results.name: Cassoulet de Toulouse
results.short_description: Hearty slow-cooked stew of white haricot beans, duck confit, Toulouse sausage, and pork cuts, simmered in a cassole (earthenware pot from nearby Issel). The Toulouse version is one of three canonical recipes (alongside Castelnaudary and Carcassonne) and is distinguished by its use of duck confit and saucisse de Toulouse.

results.name: Saucisse de Toulouse
results.short_description: Thick, coarsely ground pork sausage (75 % lean shoulder/ham, 25 % fat) seasoned with salt and pepper. Sold in a continuous coil. Documented on Toulouse market stalls since the 18th century; awarded Label Rouge in 1992 and a stricter artisanal charter in 2001. A Confrérie de la Saucisse de Toulouse holds an annual competition.
results.strength_of_local_association: ★★★★★ — Bears the city's name; iconic product

results.name: Violette de Toulouse
results.short_description: Crystallised violet flowers and violet-flavoured sweets, chocolates, mustards, jams, syrups, and liqueurs. Violet cultivation in Toulouse began c. 1850; at its peak 600 families grew the flower. "Violette de Toulouse" is now a registered trademark. The city hosts an annual violet festival in February.

results.name: Fénétra
results.short_description: Traditional Toulousain tart filled with apricot jam, candied lemon peel, and almond meringue. Its name also lends itself to the Grand Fénétra, a major annual folk festival in Toulouse.

results.name: Cachou Lajaunie
results.short_description: Small black square pastilles flavoured with liquorice and catechu plant extract, invented in 1880 by Toulouse pharmacist Léon Lajaunie. Produced in the Fontaine-Lestang quarter of Toulouse for 145 years (up to 18 tonnes/year). Production was halted in early 2025 by owner Perfetti Van Melle; a petition to save them gathered over 46,000 signatures.

results.name: Brique du Capitole
results.short_description: A praline-filled layered bonbon shaped like the iconic brique foraine (pink brick) that gives Toulouse its "Ville Rose" nickname. Created in 1951 by the Nougalet chocolate-confectionery house in Toulouse. Sold in a small brick-shaped cardboard box.
